Combinatorial optimization is the study of selecting an optimal subset from a finite set of items, and here it is applied to model non-additive interactions where a subset's value is not simply the sum of its parts. This work offers a novel mathematical reformulation of attention that preserves causal masking and the standard Transformer decoder structure while showing empirical gains over matched softmax attention. If validated, it could lead to more efficient and robust attention mechanisms for language modeling, particularly in multilingual and byte-level settings. The segment integrals have closed forms in exponential moments, yielding analytically differentiable attention without numerical quadrature, and the operator preserves normalized nonnegative effective weights. The experiments are controlled byte-level and multilingual evaluations, but the work is limited to an arXiv preprint with no community discussion provided.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 27, 04:00

**Background**: Standard Transformer attention computes a softmax over dot-product scores between queries and keys, then uses those weights to aggregate value vectors at discrete token positions. Continuum Attention instead treats neighboring key and value vectors as defining a continuous piecewise linear memory curve, and each query retrieves information by integrating an exponential relevance density along its visible prefix. This replaces the discrete softmax-weighted sum with an exact integral that has a closed-form solution, while still fitting into the standard decoder framework.

Researchers introduced DialFork, the first benchmark to measure procedural hallucination in conversational agents by forking conformant dialogues and injecting controlled deviations, yielding 36,278 dialogues across 24 tasks in 12 domains. The benchmark defines three evaluation tasks at different granularities and proposes dialog-flow-aware metrics FlowKL and FlowScore, with FlowScore significantly outperforming baselines across seven encoders. This work addresses a previously overlooked failure mode—procedural hallucination—where agents produce fluent, factually plausible utterances but deviate from the intended conversational process, which is critical for deploying reliable LLM agents in procedural tasks like booking or troubleshooting. It shifts evaluation focus from content factuality to procedural adherence, potentially impacting how conversational agents are monitored and guarded in real-world applications. The dataset was validated by 30 human annotators, and the benchmark includes three tasks: monitoring deployed agents, procedural retrieval, and real-time guardrails. FlowScore, a dialog-flow-aware metric, compares dialogues by how they unfold rather than their content, demonstrating that semantic similarity is no substitute for procedural similarity.

## [RiskCueBench Reveals Safety Miscalibration in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22425) ⭐️ 7.0/10

The paper introduces RiskCueBench, a recoverability-controlled benchmark that separates intent understanding from response-level safety behavior, and finds that more contextualized prompts shift models toward less safe responses. Specifically, when conditioning on pairs where both surface forms are recoverable, refusal rate and global safety score decrease by 0.175 and 0.440, respectively, and unsafe cooperation increases by 0.107. This work highlights a critical flaw in current safety evaluations that only score final responses, conflating intent understanding with safety behavior. It motivates new evaluation protocols that report response behavior conditional on semantic recoverability, which could lead to more robust alignment and safer LLM deployments. RiskCueBench contains 160 latent intents and 640 abstract non-operational surface prompts across eight risk categories, covering 25 completed model groups and 32,000 successful model outputs with rubric-adjudicated labels. The analysis uses paired bootstrap estimates and mixed effects modeling to show that safety behavior can be miscalibrated to surface form even after intent is recovered.

## [Learner-free swarm self-organizes to reinforcement learning equilibrium](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25113) ⭐️ 7.0/10

A new arXiv preprint (2610.25113v3) shows that a minimal foraging swarm using Lévy flights, threshold recruitment, and density-dependent dispersal self-organizes to the ideal-free distribution (IFD) equilibrium of a congestion game with a matching slope of 0.94, without any learner, reward signal, or trained parameters. Ablating the coupling between recruitment and movement collapses the match to a slope of 0.08, and the swarm's allocation gradient (~1) matches the IFD more faithfully than PPO learners (0.69–0.91) trained in the same sensing-limited environment. This result bridges swarm intelligence and reinforcement learning by showing that the physics of a simple self-organizing swarm can reach the equilibrium that RL seeks, suggesting that learning may buy precision and transfer rather than a fundamentally better allocation. It could influence the design of decentralized multi-agent systems where training or reward signals are impractical. The swarm attains the shape of the equilibrium but not the exact equilibrium, remaining measurably exploitable with a Nash gap of 0.58 versus ~0.01 for a converged learner; it ties the best learner's harvest where resources are clustered (both plateau at ~0.80 of an oracle ceiling) but collects less where resources are scarce (0.33 vs 0.22). The authors emphasize that the reinforcement learning is at the level of the problem and the allocation reached, not the micro-rule, and that neither message passing nor a centralized critic exceeds the swarm at this budget.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 27, 04:00

**Background**: The explore-exploit trade-off is a core challenge in reinforcement learning, and in multi-agent resource-sharing settings the optimum is an equilibrium allocation known as the ideal-free distribution (IFD), the Nash equilibrium of a congestion game. The Lévy flight foraging hypothesis proposes that heavy-tailed random walks optimize search efficiency when resource locations are unknown, and threshold recruitment models describe how decentralized agents can allocate labor via internal response thresholds. This paper combines these ideas to show that a minimal swarm can self-organize to the IFD without any learning mechanism.

## [SWIFT: Self-guided weak-to-strong diffusion training via target extrapolation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25844) ⭐️ 7.0/10

SWIFT introduces a self-guided training method that uses a frozen weak denoiser to extrapolate the clean regression target away from the weak prediction, amplifying underfit components without adding inference overhead. The weak guide can be an early training checkpoint, requires no backpropagation during main-model training, and is discarded afterward, with theoretical justification via RKHS spectral analysis. This method improves diffusion model quality without extra sampling cost, potentially reducing total training compute—surpassing baseline FID with roughly half the compute on ImageNet-256—and could benefit ML researchers and practitioners training generative models. SWIFT retains the original sampler and supports both conditional and unconditional generation without label dropout or an unconditional branch; on RAEv2 it achieves FID 1.15 without inference-time guidance and 0.99 with guidance, with experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256 across model scales.

The authors propose ZoE (Z-scores over Evidence), a scoring rule that scores documentation and usage separately so that tools without usage retain their documentation score. ## [Optimal Correction Sets for Provable Redress of Contestable Causal Discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33138) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper formulates the repair of conflicting conditional-independence (CI) facts in causal discovery as a minimum-cost correction problem and implements it in Answer Set Programming (ASP), building on Causal Assumption-based Argumentation (Causal ABA). It provides a compact ASP encoding with soundness and completeness guarantees, a two-way projection correspondence between optimal stable models and minimum-cost correction sets, and formally guaranteed redress under user contestations; the resulting system, OptABA-PC, retains more correct facts and improves graph reconstruction over Causal ABA on common benchmarks. This work makes constraint-based causal discovery contestable and auditable by providing an inspectable repair object, conflict-based justifications, and a predictable revision procedure, which matters for explainable AI and for domains where causal conclusions must be defended to users or regulators. It also advances the integration of argumentation and constraint solving for trustworthy causal inference. The approach guarantees fidelity to retained facts, subset-minimality and cost optimality of the repair, and formally guaranteed redress under user contestations; however, it is an arXiv preprint evaluated on standard benchmarks, and its scalability to large CI sets and real-world expert contestation workflows remains to be tested.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 27, 04:00

**Background**: Constraint-based causal discovery algorithms such as PC and FCI rely on conditional-independence (CI) tests to prune and orient edges in a causal graph, but in finite samples these tests can conflict, leaving no graph that satisfies all of them. Causal Assumption-based Argumentation (Causal ABA) treats CI tests as defeasible assumptions and offers correspondence guarantees with a subset of them, but its existing repair procedure releases facts heuristically without a formal response to user contestation. Answer Set Programming (ASP) is a declarative programming paradigm for NP-hard search problems based on stable model semantics, and it is used here to encode causal consistency and compute optimal repairs.

## [InfiniteWorld Benchmark Tests If Video-Language Models Trust Visual Evidence Over Physics Priors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33777) ⭐️ 6.0/10

InfiniteWorld introduces a benchmark that pairs physical-reasoning questions with simulator videos whose physical parameters are systematically altered, evaluating video-language models under five matched input settings including text-only and ordered/shuffled observations from simulator and translated videos. The results reveal a persistent preference for familiar physical rules: models perform well on Earth-normal questions but poorly recognize altered dynamics, and often give Earth-normal answers even when observed physics changes. This benchmark addresses a key gap in physical reasoning evaluation by isolating whether models rely on visual evidence or prior expectations, which is crucial for deploying video-language models in real-world scenarios where physics may differ from Earth norms. It provides a diagnostic tool that could drive improvements in model robustness and generalization. The benchmark includes five tasks—law identification, parameter estimation, temporal reasoning, analytic counterfactual comparison, and law induction—and uses a generation pipeline connecting simulation, scene screening, paired video translation, question construction, and input checks. Task scores and semantic agreement further distinguish matching physical factors from matching their amount, and correct answers from repeated errors.

Existing benchmarks measure overall physical capabilities but don't reveal whether models follow visual evidence when familiar rules no longer apply. A new arXiv paper introduces SPAFT, a structured pruning-and-fine-tuning framework that constrains adaptive fine-tuning to a compact, task-relevant parameter space based on parameter importance and structural redundancy. Across four PPG foundation models, five benchmark datasets, and ten downstream tasks, SPAFT achieves win rates of 82.8% on regression and 87.5% on classification tasks. PPG foundation models often fail to outperform general-purpose time-series models on real-world wearable data even after full fine-tuning, so this prune-then-finetune approach could make them viable for clinical deployment and personalized wearable health monitoring. It also offers a practical adaptation recipe for a niche but growing area of biosignal foundation models. The method is motivated by empirical findings that pretrained PPG models exhibit inherent sparsity and computational redundancy, activating task-relevant network substructures for different prediction tasks. The evaluation spans four PPG foundation models, five benchmark datasets, and ten downstream tasks, though the paper is an incremental applied contribution and no community discussion is available to validate impact.

## [Fed-Universe proposes S-G-T-H stack for negotiated alignment in federated learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34009) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Fed-Universe introduces a Semantic-Geometric-Topological-Human (S-G-T-H) architecture that replaces passive averaging in federated learning with active negotiation, incorporating an edge-capable LLM for semantic translation, geometric quality assurance via a cosine similarity gate, topological Pareto control with a sensitivity-based knee point, and a cognitive twin dynamic for human interaction. A proof-of-concept on a binational synthetic clinical network showed a minority node with less than 3% data volume achieved utility parity, reducing loss from 0.857 to 0.340 alongside dominant hubs. This work addresses a known limitation of federated learning—the suppression of minority data under cross-site heterogeneity—by moving beyond one-size-fits-all global averaging. If validated at scale, the framework could improve fairness and representation in decentralized AI systems, particularly in healthcare and other domains where small institutions or rare populations are easily overshadowed. The geometric layer maps statistical parameters to a physically interpretable quality domain and uses a cosine similarity gate to retain minority updates based on physical geometry rather than statistical proximity. The topological layer identifies a sensitivity-based knee point (lambda_k) to balance multi-objective aggregation, and the human layer operationalizes a cognitive twin to adapt interaction modes; however, the abstract is truncated and empirical validation is limited to the S-G-T core on a synthetic clinical network, with no results for the H-layer or real-world deployment.

**Background**: Federated learning trains a shared model across decentralized devices without centralizing data, typically by averaging local model updates. This approach implicitly optimizes for global means, which can suppress minority clients whose data distributions differ significantly from the majority—a problem known as one-size-fits-all. Cosine similarity is a common metric for comparing vectors by direction, often used in federated learning to assess model update quality. Pareto knee points help balance multiple objectives by finding a trade-off point where further improvement in one objective requires sacrificing another.

## [R2A-Sales benchmark exposes large rule-to-action gap in LLM sales agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34185) ⭐️ 6.0/10

R2A-Sales introduces a policy-atom-matched benchmark that pairs static policy probes with multi-turn sales scenarios sharing identical policy atoms, facts, and tool contracts, and reports a matched gap G = K − A between static compliance K and grounded action compliance A. In a confirmatory study of 21,888 runs across 12 configurations, static compliance was near ceiling (89.9%–99.1%) while action compliance was only 3.0%–17.3%, yielding gaps of 80.4–92.5 percentage points. This work shows that evaluating sales agents on rule recital or task success alone dramatically overstates their reliability, since models that can state a policy often fail to take compliant, tool-grounded actions under commercial pressure. It argues that agent evaluation should focus on committed actions verified by a code-owned ledger, which has direct implications for deploying LLM agents in regulated, customer-facing domains. The frozen release spans three controlled Chinese-language sales domains, 24 policy atoms, 42 semantic cores, and 2,016 matched pairs; the interactive arm uses a code-owned ledger to verify committed tool effects and terminal states, giving no credit for unsupported action claims. Because action compliance A also requires safe termination, the gap G upper-bounds rule-to-action degradation rather than isolating commercial pressure alone, and no prompt-only treatment dominated all metrics.

R2A-Sales addresses this by matching each static policy question with an interactive scenario built from the same policy content, so any performance difference can be attributed to the rule-to-action gap rather than to mismatched policy text.

MultiEvoSkill introduces a skill-optimization framework that compiles skill documents into typed graphs and evolves them through a heterogeneous multi-agent system with structure-aware debate, aiming to improve cross-model generalization for frozen LLM agents. The framework consists of three components: a skill compiler, a heterogeneous agent system for revision proposals, and a structure-aware debate and evolution mechanism with multi-dimensional gating. This work addresses a key limitation in current skill generators: skills authored from a single human or model perspective may not transfer well to other LLM backbones, and sequential prose descriptions fail to capture parallel branches and dependencies. By enabling graph-structured skill evolution, MultiEvoSkill could lead to more generalizable and reusable skill artifacts for frozen agents, potentially impacting how agent skills are designed and optimized across different models. The skill compiler casts skills as typed graphs with tailored operators to produce a compact representation with explicit procedural topology, while the evolution mechanism organizes candidate edits into a heterogeneous graph and resolves them under dependency and importance constraints. Multi-dimensional gating ensures information gain and topological correctness at each evolution step, and the system converges to an optimal skill at a consistent state; however, the abstract is truncated and no empirical results or community discussion are yet available.

The paper introduces a linear reparametrization of PROMETHEE II net flow scores based on weighted preference increments, yielding a linear expression that clarifies how weights and preference functions interact. Building on this, it derives linear optimization models for three settings: minimizing weight deviations with variable preference functions, minimizing deviations over all preference parameters, and multiple decision-maker consensus analysis with objectives based on total or maximal individual deviation. This work extends PROMETHEE-based sensitivity and consensus analysis beyond weight-only adjustments, showing that allowing preference functions to vary can dramatically change inverse-analysis conclusions. It provides a more comprehensive framework for group decision making and could impact how multi-criteria decision models are calibrated and agreed upon in practice. The linear reparametrization expresses net flows as a linear function of weighted preference increments over observed performance differences, enabling linear programming formulations. An illustrative example demonstrates that weight-only models can lead to misleading conclusions and that the proposed group formulations distinguish efficient consensuses from fairer ones.

## [Arya Forge Audits Financial Instruction Data Validity and Release Approval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34778) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Arya Forge introduces a system that combines typed records, current-content checks, and approval coverage bound to a dataset manifest to separate content validity from permission to release financial instruction data. Evaluated on 100,000 synthetic records and 240 release scenarios, it rejected all injected numeric faults and policy holds while retaining 220 of 240 clean controls. This work addresses a critical gap in financial data governance by formalizing the distinction between data correctness and release authorization, which could help organizations enforce stricter producer contracts and audit trails. It matters for financial data engineers and compliance teams building pipelines where regulatory and internal policies require explicit approval before data is promoted. The evaluation shows a tradeoff: adding financial and release-record checks lost all tested cash-conversion-cycle examples among the 20 rejected clean controls, and changes to external evidence after binding fall outside ordinary Gold promotion checks. The authors caution that results apply only to the tested implementation and workloads and do not establish general financial correctness or authenticated approval.

## [SEAC: Experience-Conditioned Policy for Stop-or-Clarify Fact Verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34941) ⭐️ 6.0/10

A new arXiv preprint (2610.34941) introduces Sequential Experience-Adaptive Clarification (SEAC), a lightweight evidence-acquisition policy that wraps a fixed fact verifier and decides whether to stop or request clarification for each claim. SEAC combines stop risk with an observational clarification-utility estimate derived from earlier executed trajectories, and it improves mean accuracy and macro-F1 over fact-verification and active-retrieval baselines on SciFact, LIAR, and FEVER. Most fact-verification benchmarks only score the final label, but real interactive verifiers must decide when the available evidence is sufficient, so this intermediate stop-or-clarify decision directly affects accuracy and cost. SEAC's label-free decision state and experience-based utility estimate offer a practical way to add selective clarification to existing verifiers without retraining them. SEAC retrieves evidence, runs the fixed verifier, forms a label-free decision state, and requests clarification only when the combined stop-risk and clarification-utility score exceeds the action cost and decision threshold. Equal-budget and formula-level diagnostics support selective clarification as a contributor to the gain, but the small SciFact split leaves its paired improvement inconclusive.

## [Diagnostic Protocol Separates Parameter Sharing from Graph Edges in GNN Load Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35074) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper proposes a diagnostic protocol that compares a GNN forecaster against three reference models—a per-node network, a shared network without neighbors, and the same GNN with edges removed—plus degree-preserving rewiring to test whether neighbor identity matters. Applied to regional load in France, UK low-voltage feeders, and a public client consumption dataset, it finds that parameter sharing often recovers most of the error gap (about two-thirds on feeders), while the gain from edges is smaller and largely disappears under rewiring. This work gives practitioners a concrete method to decide whether maintaining a graph is justified, potentially saving effort and complexity in load forecasting pipelines. It also cautions against crediting performance gains to graph structure without proper ablation, which could influence how GNN-based forecasting systems are designed and evaluated. On the UK feeders, parameter sharing recovers about two-thirds of the gap between node-specific models and GNNs, and adding edges yields a smaller gain of which half or more disappears under degree-preserving rewiring. On the client series, the neighbor mean degrades the per-node model on shorter windows and the edges' gain is not consistently distinguishable from zero; a synthetic study suggests noisy local measurements are one regime where neighbors help.

## [MuSID-KD: Multi-Granularity Distillation for Semantic-ID Generative Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35218) ⭐️ 6.0/10

MuSID-KD introduces a knowledge distillation framework that combines Hierarchical Candidate Distribution Alignment (HCDA) and Ranking Impact Guided Levelwise Distillation (RIGD) to train lightweight students for generative recommendation with semantic IDs. HCDA aligns candidate distributions at successive SID-prefix levels, while RIGD allocates supervision based on each SID position's impact on pairwise ranking loss. Generative recommendation with semantic IDs suffers from high inference cost due to autoregressive decoding over multiple SID positions, and this work offers a way to reduce that cost without changing the student's online inference architecture. It could make such recommenders more practical for latency-sensitive deployment in real systems. The method targets two limitations of conventional distillation: item-level alignment may not preserve the teacher's ranking of candidate groups sharing SID prefixes, and uniform alignment across SID positions ignores differing effects on final item ranking. Experiments on real-world datasets with three lightweight student architectures show improved accuracy and better alignment of prefix marginals and pairwise rankings, with code released anonymously.

## [RSIV-Harness: Recursive Self-Improvement for Text-to-Visualization Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35316) ⭐️ 6.0/10

RSIV-Harness introduces a recursive self-improvement framework that keeps the language model weights fixed while revising the surrounding agent harness based on the agent's own failure traces. A single round of improvement boosts all six evaluation metrics, with executability up 28.02 points and chart structure up 34.01 points on the new ODAC-Vis benchmark of 640 open-domain, ambiguous, and conversational text-to-visualization tasks. This work shows that agents can learn from their own failures without retraining the underlying model, offering a practical path to more robust text-to-visualization assistants that handle ambiguous, multi-turn data requests. It also introduces a benchmark that jointly evaluates open-domain data discovery, ambiguity resolution, and executable chart generation, which could standardize evaluation in this niche but growing area. The framework uses a four-layer process with anchor and memory checks to validate proposed harness revisions, refining those that pass and restoring the best validated harness otherwise, balancing flexibility with stability. The ODAC-Vis benchmark contains 640 tasks designed to test open-domain data discovery, ambiguity resolution, multi-turn refinement, and executable chart generation.

## [AdaTrendLike: Adaptive Detrending and Trend Likelihood Scoring for Time Series Anomaly Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35400) ⭐️ 6.0/10

AdaTrendLike is a new time-series anomaly detection framework that adaptively decomposes series into trend and detrended components, then scores anomalies by measuring the likelihood of observed trends under a learned distribution. It introduces Standardization Embedding, AdaDetrending, TrendEst, and TrendLike modules, and uses FFT with a complex-valued CNN to model periodic patterns in the detrended component. Existing anomaly detection methods often focus on reconstruction or forecasting and overlook trend dynamics, which are a major source of non-stationarity in Industrial IoT data. By directly modeling trend likelihoods, AdaTrendLike improves detection performance and provides feature-level interpretability, which could benefit industrial monitoring and predictive maintenance applications. The detrended component is processed via FFT and a complex-valued CNN to learn normal periodic patterns, while the trend component's distribution is modeled by TrendEst. Experiments on five public benchmark datasets show consistent outperformance over state-of-the-art TSAD methods, though the paper does not detail computational overhead or scalability to very large IIoT deployments.

**Background**: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) aims to identify unusual patterns in sequential data, and is critical for Industrial IoT where sensor data is often non-stationary—meaning its statistical properties like mean and variance change over time. Non-stationarity often arises from trends, which many existing methods ignore by focusing on reconstruction or forecasting. The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is an efficient algorithm for converting signals into the frequency domain, and complex-valued CNNs extend standard CNNs to handle complex numbers, useful for processing frequency-domain representations with phase information.

SAP-ViT replaces the global CLS token in Vision Transformers with direct aggregation of last-layer patch embeddings, making class predictions decomposable into patch-level contributions during the forward pass. It also introduces sparsity regularization on patch weights and an input-space back-mapping mechanism to trace influential output patches back to input patches. This work addresses the poor alignment between ViT's global CLS token and the local interpretability required in medical imaging, offering a favorable trade-off between accuracy and interpretability. It could benefit clinical adoption of AI by providing consistent patch-level explanations across different imaging modalities. The method is evaluated qualitatively and quantitatively on multiple medical image classification datasets across modalities, with ablations showing that both sparsity regularization and the alignment component of back-mapping improve explanation quality. However, the approach is an incremental architectural modification and its clinical validity still requires further validation.

EvoRouter introduces a self-evolving multi-agent routing framework that uses a dedicated expert to synthesize reusable conditional routing insights from configuration trajectories, and a privileged teacher to provide dense token-level supervision via on-policy distillation. Evaluated on 19 in-domain datasets across five domains and two out-of-domain benchmarks, it achieves 68.69% average in-domain accuracy, outperforming the strongest routing baseline by 7.23 percentage points while cutting inference compute cost by 50.95%. Configuring LLM multi-agent systems at scale involves a combinatorial space of model choices, collaboration modes, agent counts, interaction rounds, and skills, so a router that jointly optimizes accuracy and cost could make multi-agent deployments far more practical. The reported 50.95% compute reduction alongside a 7.23-point accuracy gain suggests routing policies can be learned more sample-efficiently, which matters for teams serving web queries at scale. The framework combines insight-guided on-policy distillation with cost-aware reinforcement learning, where the updated routing policy generates new trajectories that feed back into subsequent insight extraction, forming an execution-driven self-improvement loop. The code is open-sourced at https://github.com/CenYangtze/EvoRouter, though the work is an early arXiv preprint with no independent validation yet.

## [CLOSURE: Cross-Channel Closure for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35753) ⭐️ 6.0/10

CLOSURE introduces a new anomaly detection framework that separates recoverability and cross-channel consistency into two independently learned prediction tasks, arguing that reconstruction residuals alone cannot detect coordinated transitions or silent sensor drift. The recoverability task uses a diffusion reconstructor conditioned on a discrete memory of normal temporal bases, while the consistency task employs a relation-closure operator that predicts each channel exclusively from the others with sparse signed gates. This work challenges the dominant reconstruction-residual paradigm in unsupervised multivariate time series anomaly detection, which is widely used in industrial monitoring and server cluster management. If validated, the cross-channel closure criterion could improve detection of subtle anomalies like coordinated operating transitions and sensor drift that current methods miss. The relation-closure operator withholds the target channel's own trajectory and uses sparse signed gates to decide which peer channels are actually used, and the two scores are reconciled only through calibration on normal data. The abstract is truncated before results are shown, and no community discussion or validation is available yet.

A controlled study on Taiwanese historical question answering compared agentic RAG and static RAG sharing the same generator and hybrid retrieval backend. Although aggregate scores were similar, the two pipelines produced different answers on 70.83% of questions, and a post-hoc response selector recovered 60.34% of the oracle headroom (0.2417 composite-score gain). For RAG practitioners, this points toward question-level selection or routing between pipelines rather than chasing a single universally superior architecture. The study is limited to the narrow domain of Taiwanese historical QA, and the selector's gains are measured against an oracle that always picks the better of the two responses. ## [TraceQuery: Learning What to Recompute in Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33008) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper proposes TraceQuery, a lightweight sparse decoding framework for diffusion large language models (dLLMs) that uses full-denoising trajectories to supervise which unresolved token positions should receive limited fresh computation, rather than broadly repairing representation error. It predicts a small set of near-future trajectory-relevant positions, queries only those candidates, and lets the backbone select which one to commit from their fresh predictions. This approach delivers the strongest quality-computation trade-off among cache-based methods, sustaining high accuracy with substantially fewer fresh token computations, and generalizes across tasks, model variants, and families. It could make diffusion LLM inference significantly more efficient, lowering deployment costs for this emerging class of models. TraceQuery is trained using full-denoising trajectories as supervision and operates as a sparse decoding framework that queries only a small set of candidate positions per step. The code is available at https://github.com/fish1928/tracequery.git, and the method is presented as an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2610.33008).

Researchers introduce SUDO, the Scholarly Upper Discourse Ontology, which models how knowledge elements are organized into a paper's research narrative, moving beyond concept-centric and statement-centric paradigms. The ontology enables bottom-up construction of a paper's scholarly discourse and connects research narratives across papers into a global discourse, with demonstrated improvements on an LLM-based scientific QA task. This work addresses a key limitation of existing scholarly knowledge graphs, which often reflect a pre-chosen extraction target rather than how a paper actually constructs knowledge. By providing a general, linguistically grounded structure for discourse, SUDO could improve literature search, scientific discovery, and agent-assisted research that rely on richer knowledge representations. SUDO uses linguistic principles that generalize across fields and tasks, allowing each publication's discourse to be represented as a coherent, source-grounded structure without discarding local context or provenance. The authors demonstrate its capabilities across a comprehensive suite of scholarly knowledge-modeling use cases and report performance improvements on a downstream LLM-based scientific QA task.

## [Feature Scaling Outweighs Architecture Choice in Low-Resource Respiratory Screening](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33030) ⭐️ 6.0/10

A pre-registered study comparing classical and deep classifiers on a five-class respiratory sound corpus of 1,211 clips from 201 patient groups found that standardizing features for an SVM raised its macro recall from 0.51 to 0.78, a 27-point swing larger than any difference between model families. The SVM over 30 summary features matched or slightly exceeded a 1.13M-parameter CNN-RNN (0.75–0.77 macro recall), and no significant difference between model families was resolved. This finding suggests that for low-resource clinical settings without GPUs or reliable connectivity, a well-preprocessed classical model can be as effective as a deep model while avoiding a 449 MB PyTorch runtime, making deployment far more practical. It also highlights that routine preprocessing steps may matter more than architectural sophistication in small medical audio datasets. The study used patient-grouped cross-validation with 25 runs per configuration and found that augmentation (SMOTE, waveform augmentation, SpecAugment) had no measurable effect, while clip-level splits inflated macro recall by 7.5–9.8 points. The authors identify a major confound: recording source is strongly tied to label (Cramer's V = 0.65 between native sampling rate and class), and clips recorded at a class's minority rate are mostly assigned to classes typical of that rate.

**Background**: Respiratory sound classification aims to automatically detect conditions like asthma, COPD, and pneumonia from recordings such as coughs or breath sounds. ## [StyleInstructCaps: A New Benchmark for Controllable Speaking-Style Captioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33036) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper formulates controllable speaking-style captioning (SSC) as an instruction-following audio-language task and introduces StyleInstructCaps, the first standardized benchmark for dimension-specific style captions. It provides a dataset and evaluation framework that measures metadata groundedness, hallucination, instruction-following ability, generalization to unseen instructions and audio datasets, and speaker-style consistency. This benchmark fills a gap in the unified formulation of controllable SSC, enabling systematic evaluation of audio-language models on paralinguistic understanding. It could impact research in conversational AI, controllable speech generation, and audio annotation by providing a standardized way to assess and improve model performance. Evaluating nine state-of-the-art audio-language models, the authors find that strong instruction-following ability does not necessarily imply grounded speaking-style understanding, and that SSC-specific instruction-diverse training substantially improves groundedness, controllability, and speaker consistency.

## [GMoE-FTI: Universal Facial Template Inversion via Genuine Mixture-of-Experts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33055) ⭐️ 6.0/10

Researchers proposed GMoE-FTI, a universal facial template inversion framework that uses a genuine mixture-of-experts (MoE) mechanism to reconstruct identity-consistent faces from five categories of facial templates. Evaluated on seven unseen template types, it achieves an average 40% TAR improvement over state-of-the-art methods, with FAPD and FAPC each reduced by 2%. This work exposes a significant biometric privacy risk: even templates from unseen extractors can be inverted into recognizable faces, undermining the assumption that storing only templates protects user privacy. It also demonstrates a practical application of genuine MoE for heterogeneous domain generalization, which could inspire similar universal inversion or adaptation frameworks. The framework classifies template extractors into five distribution categories (unit-sphere, angle-linear, strict unit-sphere, cone-shaped, anuniform hypersphere) and trains five mapping experts plus a matching module in three stages: independent training, collaborative inference to generate latent codes for StyleGAN3, and end-to-end joint fine-tuning. Evaluations on LFW show generalization to seven unseen template types including AdaFace, CosFace, CurricularFace, ElasticFace, SphereFace2, SphereFace-R, and TransFace.

DRA-SAM introduces a disagreement-driven active inference framework that uses a lightweight EvidenceScorer and a training-free LOOK policy to selectively re-infer ambiguous regions for referring segmentation in low-altitude drone imagery. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on six of seven metrics on RIS-LAD and UAVid-RIS, improving the SAM3-I baseline from 49.55 to 52.34 mIoU on RIS-LAD. It could benefit applications like aerial surveillance, search and rescue, and precision agriculture where accurate small-object segmentation is critical. The method uses a benchmark-adapted SAM3-I backbone and a training-free LOOK policy that balances belief-weighted candidate competition and unresolved-region coverage. For inter-subject decoding, a target-guided least-squares transformation aligns source trials using one labeled target trial per class; ablation studies show that fixing the estimated TDCA projection outperforms optimizing it from analytical or random initialization.

## [ProtoEEG aligns EEG and images via a shared 64-prototype codebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33065) ⭐️ 6.0/10

ProtoEEG reformulates EEG-image alignment as a soft composition over a shared learnable visual codebook of K=64 prototypes, where a trainable EEG encoder and a frozen visual teacher both output assignment distributions over the same prototypes. It achieves 64.0% Top-1 and 91.5% Top-5 on THINGS-EEG2 200-way retrieval across five seeds, and 44.8% Top-1 and 73.8% Top-5 on 80-way EEG-ImageNet retrieval, while ranking first on all seven reconstruction metrics. This work shows that structured alignment targets can be a practical alternative to simply scaling encoder or teacher capacity, which is significant for noisy, low-resolution EEG signals that cannot support dense image embeddings. It could benefit brain-computer interface and neuroscience researchers working on visual decoding and image reconstruction from brain activity. Ablations show that removing prototype contrast lowers Top-1 by 56.9 percentage points, and shuffling prototype identities collapses Top-1 to 0.5%, confirming the codebook bottleneck is genuinely used. Prototype analyses reveal distributed assignments and broad codebook use rather than one-prototype routing, and the shared assignment profile enables direct tests via prototype retention, random selection, and identity shuffling.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 27, 04:00

**Background**: EEG visual decoding aims to infer what a person is seeing from scalp recordings, but EEG is noisy, spatially coarse, and variable across trials and subjects. Most existing systems align each EEG trial with a dense image embedding from a vision model, yet that embedding mixes semantic content with instance-specific texture, pose, and background, demanding details absent from EEG. Prototype learning, common in interpretable deep networks, represents inputs as combinations of learned reference patterns, and ProtoEEG applies this idea as a cross-modal bottleneck between EEG and visual representations.

A new arXiv paper (2610.33075) diagnoses evidence misgrounding in multimodal knowledge editing, where edits yield correct answers but rely on incidental context, and introduces WaterBird-Edit, a controlled analysis set that decouples bird habitat labels from background. The authors propose VICE (Visual In-Context Editing), a retrieval-based framework that stores edits in external memory and applies them via visual in-context demonstrations, showing strong lifelong editing performance on three benchmarks and reduced sensitivity to background shifts. By providing a diagnostic dataset and a retrieval-based mitigation, it pushes the field toward more robust and trustworthy editing methods for MLLMs. VICE stores edits in external memory and applies them through visual in-context demonstrations designed to expose task-relevant evidence, rather than modifying model parameters. The WaterBird-Edit set specifically measures whether edited predictions remain stable when target evidence is preserved but background changes, and code and dataset are released on GitHub.

## [ESCal: Error-Subspace Calibration for Multi-Task Model Merging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33483) ⭐️ 6.0/10

ESCal is a post-merging calibration framework that derives low-dimensional error subspaces from weight differences between expert and merged models, then learns only linear bridge modules to project merged representations into these subspaces and apply additive corrections. Experiments on vision and natural language understanding benchmarks show improved merged-model performance across architectures and merging methods using a small per-task calibration set. Model merging is an increasingly popular way to combine task-specific experts without joint training, but merged models often underperform the originals. ESCal offers a parameter-efficient post-hoc fix that could make merged models more faithful to expert behavior, benefiting practitioners who deploy multi-task models under compute or data constraints. The subspace bases are fixed, so calibration only learns linear maps, keeping the method parameter-efficient. The approach is evaluated on both vision and NLU benchmarks and is designed to work with diverse architectures and merging methods, though it remains an incremental research contribution without community validation yet.

The paper introduces Factorized Write Routing (FWR), a mechanism that first decides whether to keep or skip each token and then chooses a fixed or token-adaptive number of memory slots to update. Across ten seeds on two synthetic long-context tasks, it finds a density-dependent reversal: always writing wins on dense Feature Recall (0.472 vs 0.337), while learned selective writing wins on sparse-fact Passkey (0.222 vs 0.048). It suggests that long-context memory systems should adapt their writing policy to the sparsity of relevant facts, which could inform the design of more efficient and accurate models. The adaptive slot-allocation rule underperforms fixed allocation under the learned gate on both tasks, and a diagnostic oracle with fact labels reaches only 0.372 on Passkey, indicating substantial headroom in filtering distractors. Evaluation is limited to two synthetic tasks, so generalization to real-world long-context benchmarks remains untested.

Logits are the pre-softmax scores a model assigns to each vocabulary token, and top-K calibration adjusts only the most likely candidates rather than the full vocabulary. GRASP introduces a group-adaptive hybrid post-training method that combines reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning in every update using only short answers, and releases the MedTerse dataset of 12.9K short-answer questions. GRASP uses RL to let the model explore its own reasoning and SFT to teach the gold answer after that reasoning, with their balance adapting to how well the model answers each question. DynEdit introduces a dynamic framework for long-sequence knowledge editing in large language models that uses token-level entropy to guide non-uniform sliding windows and token-level optimization, prioritizing difficult high-entropy regions instead of fixed chunking. Experiments on three benchmarks and two backbone models show consistent gains over competitive baselines, including up to +14.0 BLEU points on challenging paraphrase queries and near-saturated semantic scores across several knowledge domains. The method relies on the observation that high-entropy tokens are both harder to edit and more semantically important, and it combines entropy-guided non-uniform sliding with entropy-guided token-level optimization inside each window. ## [ToDoPro: Early Token Reduction for Faster Reference-Based Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34782) ⭐️ 6.0/10

ToDoPro introduces a method for early token reduction in reference-based image generation using Diffusion Transformers (DiTs). By performing a few denoising steps on spatially downsampled reference images, it probes token importance and hierarchically reduces tokens before the main denoising stage, achieving acceleration and memory savings without additional parameters or external models. This approach addresses the token explosion problem in multi-reference image generation, which causes quadratic computational complexity and high memory usage. It could enable more efficient deployment of reference-based generative models, making them practical for resource-constrained environments and potentially improving generation quality by filtering noisy tokens. The method uses a cheap probing stage with 2x downsampled images to extract token importance via the DiT itself, then applies hierarchical reduction: discarding low-importance tokens, substituting mid-importance tokens with downsampled counterparts, and keeping high-importance tokens. The paper introduces a native characterization of abductive (AXps) and contrastive (CXps) explanations directly over finite traces for Linear Temporal Logic over Finite Traces (LTLf), based on locking and unlocking time-indexed events. It proves equivalence with the classifier-based formulation and shows that CXps coincide with a recently proposed temporal causality semantics for LTLf, enabling an efficient implementation via minimal unsatisfiable cores and minimal correction sets of ASP programs. The native characterization is based on locking and unlocking time-indexed events, and the implementation leverages enumeration of minimal unsatisfiable cores and minimal correction sets in Answer Set Programming (ASP). ## [Neutral Substrates: A Design Constraint for Shared Records Under Persistent Interpretive Disagreement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14271) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper formalizes a neutral substrate design for shared accountability records that separates shared referential commitments from attributed interpretive assertions. It introduces concepts such as admissible frameworks, referential commitments, permitted attributions, interpretive non-commitment, and extension stability, and shows that under Referential Common Ground, restricting substrate-layer commitments to referential commitments or permitted attribution propositions is sufficient for semantic neutrality relative to every admissible framework. This work provides a precise conditional layer restriction and an explicit account of its semantic and scientific boundaries, which is relevant to accountability systems and data modeling where parties may persistently disagree. It offers a formal approach to designing shared records that remain neutral under interpretive disagreement, potentially impacting how accountability records are structured in multi-party systems. The essential assumption is joint compatibility of the complete referential commitment set with each admissible framework; separate compatibility of individual commitments is not sufficient, and admissible frameworks need not be mutually consistent. Furthermore, the formal referential interfaces do not independently establish identity criteria, denotation relations, attributional bases, or interpretive adequacy required by a particular application, so neutrality cannot be certified when those premises cannot be justified.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 27, 04:00

**Background**: Shared accountability records are used in systems where multiple parties need to track events, responsibilities, and causes, but they often disagree on interpretation. A neutral substrate aims to keep the record useful to all parties by separating objective referential commitments (e.g., what event occurred) from interpretive assertions (e.g., who is responsible). This paper provides a formal framework for such separation, drawing on concepts from formal methods and data modeling.

EpiPersona introduces a framework that projects noisy preference feedback into a low-dimensional persona space, aggregating similar personas into shared discrete codewords, and then couples the inferred persona representation with the current episode for episode-aware preference prediction. Experiments show it outperforms baselines, especially in hard episodic-shift scenarios and with sparse preference data. This work addresses a key challenge in pluralistic alignment: separating stable personal traits from situational factors to improve generalization across episodes. It could lead to more robust personalized reward models for LLMs, benefiting applications that require adapting to diverse individual and minority preferences. The method does not rely on predefined preference dimensions, instead learning discrete codewords to represent personas. It remains effective with sparse preference data, though the paper is an incremental research contribution without community discussion or evidence of major impact yet.

## [PREFER: Online Learning Framework for Personalized Review Summarization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05911) ⭐️ 6.0/10

PREFER introduces an online learning framework that generates personalized review summaries by modeling user preferences in a latent aspect space and iteratively refining them with feedback. Evaluated on Amazon Reviews'23, it improves preference-aligned evidence selection, and a human study shows scenario-conditioned summaries are preferred over generic ones in 69.9% of paired comparisons. This work addresses the practical problem of information overload in e-commerce by moving beyond static, generic summaries to dynamic, user-specific ones that evolve with interactions. It could benefit online shoppers and platforms by surfacing the most relevant review evidence for each individual, potentially increasing purchase confidence and satisfaction. The framework uses controlled feedback simulations and robustness checks with held-out-history, independent-embedding, and external LLM-based evaluators, but the main evaluation relies on simulated feedback rather than real user interactions. The human study is separate and focuses on scenario-conditioned summaries, not the full online learning loop.

PREFER tackles this by representing user interests in a latent aspect space—where aspects are product characteristics like battery life or build quality—and updating this representation online as the user gives feedback. ## [PRISE and NeurPRISE: Problem-Driven Scenario Reduction for Two-Stage Robust Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14494) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper introduces PRISE, a problem-driven sequential lookahead heuristic for scenario reduction in two-stage robust optimization with discrete uncertainty, and NeurPRISE, a GNN-Transformer surrogate trained via imitation learning that accelerates PRISE by 17-200x while maintaining competitive regret. Scenario reduction is critical for making two-stage robust optimization tractable, and existing methods are largely problem-agnostic; PRISE and NeurPRISE address this by incorporating problem structure and using a neural surrogate to overcome computational bottlenecks, potentially enabling broader adoption of 2RO in large-scale applications. NeurPRISE uses a GNN-Transformer backbone to encode per-scenario structure via graph convolution and cross-scenario interactions via attention, and is trained with a gain-aware ranking objective; it demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization to instances with up to 5x larger problem scales, 4x more scenarios, and distribution shifts.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 27, 04:00

**Background**: Two-stage robust optimization (2RO) is a framework for decision-making under uncertainty where some decisions are made before uncertainty is revealed and recourse decisions are made afterward. When uncertainty is discrete, the problem can be computationally prohibitive due to the large number of scenarios. Scenario reduction selects a small representative subset of scenarios to make the problem tractable, but traditional methods often ignore the problem's feasible region and recourse structure.

## [NGM: A Plug-and-Play Training-Free Memory Module for LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16893) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper proposes N-gram Memory (NGM), a training-free, plug-and-play module that reuses a backbone model's pretrained token embeddings as memory via a Causal N-Gram Encoder and a Cosine-Gated Memory Injector. Evaluated on ten benchmarks across six backbones (four Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 8B and two Llama-3.2-Instruct models at 1B and 3B), NGM consistently improves the ten-task average, including gains of 4.26 points on HumanEval, 2.41 on HumanEval+, and 6.56 on GPQA-Diamond. NGM offers a lightweight way to augment LLM memory without additional training, learned memory banks, or external retrieval infrastructure, which could lower the cost and complexity of deploying memory-augmented models. Its demonstrated gains across multiple model families and scales, plus extension to vision-language models, suggest practical value for improving reasoning and coding performance in existing backbones. The Causal N-Gram Encoder builds N-gram representations by directly aggregating pretrained token embeddings, while the Cosine-Gated Memory Injector uses cosine similarity with ReLU gating to adaptively control how much retrieved memory is injected into contextual representations. NGM also extends beyond text-only models: Qwen3-VL-2B achieves improvements across all five VLM benchmarks.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Oct 27, 04:00

**Background**: N-gram language models are classical statistical models that predict the next word based on a fixed window of previous words, and n-grams represent contiguous sequences of n items from text. Memory-augmented neural networks add an explicit external memory to standard architectures so models can read from and write to a memory bank, but many such approaches require learned memory embeddings or separate retrieval components. NGM instead repurposes the backbone's existing token embedding space as memory, avoiding extra training and architectural complexity.

The paper introduces AliO (Align Outputs), a method that reduces discrepancies between predictions for the same timestamps across lagged input sequences in both time and frequency domains, and proposes a new Time Alignment Metric (TAM) to quantify this alignment. Experiments show up to 58.2% improvement in TAM while maintaining or enhancing forecasting performance by up to 27.5%. Output alignment is a previously overlooked reliability issue in long-term time series forecasting (LTSF), where inconsistent predictions for the same timestamp can undermine trust in models used for weather forecasting and electricity planning. AliO and TAM provide a new evaluation dimension and a practical training approach that could lead to more stable and trustworthy LTSF models. AliO works by minimizing prediction discrepancies for overlapping timestamps across lagged input sequences, operating in both time and frequency domains. TAM complements existing metrics like MSE, which only measure distance to ground truth, by directly quantifying consistency among predictions.

## [Output Discipline, Not Model Scale, Limits LLM Agents on Auditable Decisions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18298) ⭐️ 6.0/10

A new arXiv paper (2610.18298v2) proposes a model-agnostic five-stage agent protocol enforced by a candidate-by-evidence falsification matrix, where at least half of candidates must be falsified before a conclusion is licensed. On the 200-case TCMEval-SDT benchmark for Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome differentiation, two years of model scaling moved zero-shot scores by only -0.03 to +0.08, while the protocol rescued undisciplined models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash: +0.267/+0.271) and cut Kimi K3's run-to-run standard deviation from 0.218 to 0.007, but cost already-disciplined models -0.087 to -0.120. The paper argues that for auditable, hypothesis-driven decision tasks, output discipline and reasoning structure—not raw model capability—set the performance floor, suggesting that agent protocol design can matter more than further model scaling. This has implications for how practitioners build reliable LLM agents in high-stakes domains such as clinical decision support, where termination, format compliance, and reproducibility are critical. The protocol's gains are sign-conditional on zero-shot output discipline: it rescues models with non-terminating reasoning or format failures but harms already-disciplined models, with ablations attributing the cost to the candidate-bounded format layer. The approach also transfers to misinformation-robust mathematical reasoning, detecting injected false premises at 89.8% recall with 6.8% false positives (MCC 0.54), and the authors show the effect is independent of injected knowledge content (protocol-knowledge decoupling).

The paper diagnoses why attention-based Pointer Networks trained with reinforcement learning degrade when generalizing across CVRP sizes, identifying node density shifts, attention dispersion, and dilution of mean-pooled graph context as key factors. It proposes a learned, permutation-invariant graph-context aggregation mechanism (weighted average and Set2Set) and an approach selector that reduces cost by up to 3.2% across seen and unseen size pairs. This work addresses a critical limitation of learning-based combinatorial optimization: the need for a single policy that generalizes across problem sizes without retraining. If validated, the proposed modifications could make RL-trained Pointer Networks more practical for real-world logistics where client counts vary, reducing the need for size-specific models. ## [WiMoT: Replay-Free Continual Wi-Fi Sensing via Moment Transport](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32660) ⭐️ 6.0/10

WiMoT introduces a replay-free continual learning method for Wi-Fi sensing that stores per-class feature means and covariances instead of raw CSI samples, and transports these statistics through an affine map on a frozen feature basis when the representation changes. On three datasets (3DO, WiMANS, Widar3.0), it achieves final accuracies of 94.02%, 89.61%, and 95.16% with at most 0.58 percentage points of forgetting. This approach addresses the privacy and storage constraints of edge Wi-Fi nodes by eliminating the need to retain raw channel state information, while still learning new rooms or users without forgetting old ones. It outperforms 21 baselines, including replay-based methods, suggesting a practical path for deploying continual Wi-Fi sensing in real-world edge environments. WiMoT uses supervised contrastive learning for new domains, a closed-form loss on stored statistics to maintain separability, and a Gaussian discriminant classifier refitted with equal weight per domain. Storing full covariances as rank-32 factors reduces moment memory to 6.4% with at most 0.49 pp accuracy loss, fitting edge-node storage budgets.

The paper introduces an entropy-calibrated linear attention module, instantiated as ELinFormer, which decomposes aggregation into a uniform component and a query-dependent correction calibrated by a query-specific temperature. It derives a second-order KL proxy from centered query-key scores and designs a smooth temperature rule to calibrate it, avoiding the full pairwise score matrix. Linear attention reduces the quadratic cost of standard attention but may bias weakly selective distributions toward uniform aggregation, weakening the amplification of high-score positions. This work offers a mechanism to preserve selective deviations in linear attention, potentially improving accuracy-memory trade-offs for multivariate and spatio-temporal time series modeling. The Taylor expansion reduces the KL proxy to squared-score energy divided by squared temperature, computable from shared products of centered keys without forming the full pairwise score matrix. Experiments on five PEMS benchmarks show competitive forecasting accuracy, and on PEMS08 the rational temperature rule and query-specific calibration achieve lower MAE than a linear rule or shared-temperature alternatives.

The model achieves state-of-the-art results on several metrics across synthetic and molecular benchmarks, with ablations isolating the contributions of the structural prior, optimal-transport coupling, and regularization terms. This work bridges flow-based generative modeling with graph limit theory by introducing graphettes as a flexible structural prior, potentially improving the generation of graphs with recurring motifs in domains like molecular design. It offers a principled way to inject domain knowledge into graph generative models, which could benefit drug discovery and materials science. The framework employs optimal transport-based coupling for topology-aware alignment and endpoint-aware and chemistry-aware regularization to preserve structural fidelity. Theoretical analysis covers coupling, invariance, and structural properties, but the approach is evaluated mainly on synthetic and molecular benchmarks, and its impact is currently limited to a specialized research niche.

A controlled study introduces RAPTOR, a pairwise-gated fusion detector, and evaluates compact HuBERT and WavLM backbones across 14 cross-domain benchmarks. ## [Multimodal Coherence Score: A New Metric for Fusion Quality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25924) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper introduces the Multimodal Coherence Score (MCS), a model-agnostic metric that decomposes multimodal coherence into identity, spatial, semantic, and decision dimensions, with weights learned via Nelder-Mead optimization. Evaluated on 1,000 Visual Genome images using DETR, CLIP, and ViLT, and validated on 150 COCO images, MCS shows higher sensitivity than task accuracy alone (Spearman rho = 0.093 vs. 0.071). Current multimodal AI systems are typically evaluated by downstream task accuracy, but high accuracy does not guarantee coherent inputs. MCS provides a way to detect data inconsistencies and diagnose fusion quality independent of any downstream model, which could help researchers build more reliable multimodal systems. MCS is lightweight, requires no human annotation, and can identify which dimension failed, not just that something broke. Perturbation experiments confirm each dimension responds independently to its failure mode with zero cross-talk, though the sensitivity improvement over task accuracy is modest.

## [AffordSim: Scalable Affordance-Aware Data Generator for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11674) ⭐️ 6.0/10

AffordSim is a new simulation-based data generator and benchmark that integrates open-vocabulary 3D affordance prediction to synthesize task-relevant scenes and region-conditioned grasps for robotic manipulation. It is instantiated as a 50-task benchmark across five robot embodiments and 500+ rigid and articulated objects, achieving 93% of the trajectory collection success rate of manual contact annotations on affordance-critical tasks and 89% on hard composite tasks. Current simulation data generators rely on generic grasp estimators that ignore task semantics or on manual contact annotations that must be redone for every new object and task, limiting scalability. The pipeline takes a natural-language task description, synthesizes a task-relevant scene, emits affordance queries grounded on object surfaces, samples region-conditioned grasps, and selects executable candidates via motion planning. It also randomizes object pose, texture, lighting, image noise, and cross-viewpoint backgrounds for sim-to-real transfer, though the zero-shot real-world success of 24% indicates substantial room for improvement.

## [CoCo-LoRA: Bayesian PEFT with Audio Context for Uncertainty Estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16615) ⭐️ 6.0/10

CoCo-LoRA introduces a multimodal, uncertainty-aware parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that conditions a Bayesian low-rank adapter on both text-derived features and an audio-derived context signal to better estimate uncertainty in speech-centered text prediction tasks. The method projects a pooled audio embedding into a shared context space and adapts it through lightweight layer-wise heads, enabling depth-specific modulation of adapter uncertainty without high-dimensional multimodal fusion. This work addresses a gap in existing Bayesian PEFT methods, which are largely unimodal and fail to reflect uncertainty driven by external acoustic factors such as background noise or speaking style. By using audio as a contextual uncertainty signal rather than a fused feature stream, CoCo-LoRA offers a parameter-efficient alternative for multimodal low-resource prediction, potentially improving reliability in speech-centered applications. Stochasticity is confined to a compact latent component in the rank space, preserving PEFT scalability while producing audio-sensitive, heteroscedastic uncertainty. Evaluations across diverse tasks and backbone combinations show that CoCo-LoRA consistently matches or outperforms text-only PEFT and conventional feature-fusion transfer baselines, particularly on high-coverage labels.

## [SPECTRA: Bayesian LoRA with Cross-Attention for Multimodal Uncertainty](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16657) ⭐️ 6.0/10

SPECTRA introduces a multimodal Bayesian low-rank adaptation framework that keeps text and audio backbones frozen while confining stochasticity to a compact rank-r latent matrix inside each LoRA adapter. At each transformer layer, text-derived low-rank token features query frame-level audio embeddings via lightweight cross-attention, and the resulting acoustic context parameterizes an amortized variational posterior over the adapter latent. This work extends parameter-efficient fine-tuning beyond deterministic, unimodal settings by making audio a localized reliability signal that modulates both adaptation and confidence, which could improve trustworthiness in low-resource audio-text tasks such as emotion recognition and clinical interview prediction. It offers a principled way to decompose predictive uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components within the adapter space. Posterior prediction uses Monte Carlo adapter samples to decompose uncertainty into total, aleatoric, and adapter-space epistemic components; on IEMOCAP and clinical interview tasks SPECTRA is competitive with or improves upon text-only Bayesian PEFT and multimodal transfer-learning baselines, and modality-disagreement stress tests show mismatched audio degrades AUC, likelihood, calibration, and Brier score more than noisy but matched audio.

## [New Paper Revisits Bias in Differentiable Simulators, Proposes DDCG and IVW-H](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18161) ⭐️ 6.0/10

A new arXiv paper re-examines the bias from discontinuous dynamics in differentiable simulators and introduces DDCG, a lightweight test that switches between first-order and zeroth-order gradient estimators in nonsmooth regions using a single hyperparameter. It also presents IVW-H, a per-step inverse-variance implementation that stabilizes variance without explicit discontinuity detection and yields strong results on differentiable robotics control tasks. This work challenges the assumption that bias from discontinuities is the primary obstacle in policy gradient RL with differentiable simulators, showing that careful variance control often dominates in practical deployments. It provides a simpler, more sample-efficient alternative to prior confidence-interval-based methods, which could make differentiable simulation more accessible for robotics and control tasks. DDCG requires only a single hyperparameter and remains reliable with small samples, addressing the high noise and task-specific tuning of the REINFORCE-based detection method. IVW-H stabilizes variance per step without explicit discontinuity detection, and the paper concludes that while estimator switching improves robustness in controlled studies, variance control is often more important in practice.

**Background**: Differentiable simulators allow computing exact gradients of a policy's objective with respect to its parameters, enabling first-order policy gradient estimates that can speed up reinforcement learning compared to derivative-free zeroth-order methods like REINFORCE. However, when the simulator's dynamics contain discontinuities (e.g., contacts), first-order gradients become biased and can stall optimization. ## [CIKA uses LLMs as causal simulators to probe math reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07600) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper introduces CIKA (Causal Intervention for Knowledge Activation), a framework that uses the LLM itself as an interventional simulator: a prompt sets a concept's state to 'mastered' and the resulting change in correctness estimates the causal effect, formalized as an Interventional Capability Probe (ICP). On 67 screened problems, the ICP of the top-ranked concept (+0.219) was significantly larger than that of a negative control (+0.039; paired t-test, p < 10^-6, Cohen's d = 0.86), and analysis of 601 Omni-MATH problems showed solved problems had 6.1× higher average treatment effect (ATE) than unsolved ones (0.338 vs. 0.055). This work offers a causal, intervention-based alternative to observational methods like MCTS-based test-time search or causal graph-guided knowledge injection, which cannot distinguish genuine concept contribution from spurious associations driven by confounders such as problem difficulty. By diagnosing whether an LLM can actually use a concept (not merely possess it), CIKA could improve how we evaluate and activate latent knowledge in frozen models, with a 7B-parameter LLM achieving 69.7% on Omni-MATH-Rule and 64.0% overall, surpassing o1-mini's 60.5%. The empirical scope is limited to 67 screened problems for the main ICP validation, though the predictive analysis covers 601 Omni-MATH problems; the Causal Knowledge Activation component contributes 33.8% of correct answers on problems where the base model alone fails, demonstrating that the LLM already possessed but had not activated the requisite knowledge. The approach requires no weight updates, relying entirely on prompting to simulate interventions.

It proposes ξ-DPO, which reformulates the preference objective to minimize the distance between reward gaps and optimal margins, and redefines the reward as a ratio between chosen and rejected responses, yielding a bounded, interpretable margin ξ that cancels β and is easier to tune. Hyperparameter tuning is a major pain point in reference-free preference optimization methods like SimPO, and ξ-DPO's ability to determine ξ from the initial reward gap distribution could make alignment training more accessible and robust across datasets. The work offers a deeper understanding of β and γ's roles, potentially influencing future algorithm design in LLM alignment. ξ-DPO reformulates the objective via an equivalent transformation and defines the ratio reward margin ξ, which is bounded and interpretable, unlike SimPO's β and γ. The paper reports extensive experiments showing ξ-DPO substantially outperforms existing preference optimization methods across open benchmarks on multiple metrics, though it is an incremental improvement over SimPO.

StableHand introduces a quality-aware flow-matching framework that decomposes per-frame hand observation reliability into four channels (wrist global translation and finger articulations for each hand) and conditions a DiT-based denoiser on these signals. The method integrates quality signals into flow matching via a per-channel forward schedule, a quality-adjusted velocity target, AdaLN modulation of the DiT denoiser, and a quality-aware ODE initialization, preserving high-quality observations while reconstructing unreliable ones using a learned bimanual motion prior. Across four tasks and eleven model variants, the IWN variant achieves a macro-F1 of 0.940, a +0.036 improvement over the strongest non-IWN baseline and +0.130 on authorship detection. The released code, vocabularies, and auto-extraction recipe lower the barrier for practitioners to adopt and extend the method. The surgical feature gate is a learned per-dimension sigmoid over curated lexical indicators and the [CLS] token, and it provably degenerates to identity when features are uninformative. A random-vocabulary control shows a -0.028 average F1 drop, confirming that gains stem from lexical rather than parametric information, and the paper provides an excess-risk bound linking gate benefit to surgical feature alignment.

## [SLAB: Time-Lag-Aware Deep RL for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling in PPVC Factories](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11725) ⭐️ 6.0/10

SLAB introduces a time-lag-aware decision process for deep reinforcement learning dispatchers in PPVC module factories, where modules must wait 12–48 hours after casting, waterproofing, and painting before the next operation. Its transition releases a module only after this wait, and its reward is the decrease of a proven lower bound that includes the waits, producing schedules that avoid costly plan repair. This work addresses a real-world constraint in PPVC construction scheduling that existing learned dispatchers ignore, leading to plans that require repair and are 42% to 133% longer. By training one dispatcher on small orders that can run without a solver on production batches of 50 to 80 modules, it offers a practical path to deploying RL in module factories. On orders generated from Singapore's PPVC guidebook, one trained policy produces schedules 2.2% to 8.1% shorter than the shortest-processing-time rule at 10 to 80 modules, and at 50 and 80 modules it outperforms a time-lag memetic algorithm by 6.7% and 7.4% and constraint-programming search (given 600 s) by 6.6% and 7.6%. However, the memetic algorithm gives shorter schedules on 10-module orders and the same search given 300 s on 10- and 20-module orders.

Researchers propose SpectONet, a physics-guided spectral deep operator network that combines DeepONet with physics-informed constraints and nonuniform Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto (CGL) sensor placement to solve Euler-Bernoulli beam vibration problems. Unlike conventional DeepONet frameworks that use uniformly distributed sensors, SpectONet places branch-network inputs at nonuniform CGL nodes concentrated near domain boundaries, improving the finite-dimensional representation of boundary-sensitive responses while requiring only a limited number of inputs. The governing beam equation with initial and boundary conditions is embedded in the training objective, and the method is evaluated on three Euler-Bernoulli beam vibration problems.

The theoretical guarantees and open-source implementation make the approach accessible for broader adoption. The method implements three compensation levels in C++ (L1: frozen set with live geometry; L2: margin-gated local repair; L3: damped, projected basis), with L2 exactly reproducing the PB edge set (D=0.0000) and L1 staying within 0.6%. The recorded trajectory yields a measured 1.5× Pass-1 and 1.76× epoch speed-up, and an analytic near-tie spacing law E[m] ≈ r_k/(3k) matches measurements to 1%.

**Background**: SE(3)-equivariant neural networks are architectures that embed 3D rotational and translational symmetry, ensuring parameter efficiency and reliable generalization in 3D applications such as protein structure prediction.
